selection_rule: Every statement by an in-scope officeholder quoted in a story published on Nov. 19 or 20, 2026 in the NPR Politics and PBS NewsHour Politics feeds, as read on Nov. 20 at about 7:40 ET, less the stories earlier pages already used, plus the one transcript from the fixed transcript sources dated in that window (the White House text of the Nov. 19 U.S.-Russia-China declaration). Transcripts from Nov. 13 to 18 were searched only to confirm quotes. PBS NewsHour carries Associated Press reporting. Quotes under five words were left out, as were commentators' accounts of what an official said and statements by officials outside the offices in scope. Statements are worded as the outlet reported them; entries beginning "Reported as" are the reporter's wording.
lede: Nov. 19 and 20 brought President Trump's three-way summit with Xi Jinping and Vladimir Putin in Shenzhen, a Senate vote on ending the war in Iran, Senate passage of a bipartisan permitting bill, and a House Homeland Security Committee hearing with Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin on the FAA ground stop, recent tech outages and a reported Iranian dirty-bomb plan. This page lists what officeholders in scope were quoted saying in that coverage, 47 statements from 18 speakers.

Seventeen statements made checkable factual claims or rested on a stated factual premise. Checks against AskAmerica's warehouse found U.S. gasoline and diesel prices above their pre-war levels, CISA's workforce down about 35% since January 2025, and Oklahoma receiving about 1.6% of federal highway formula funds. A House roll call confirmed how Mullin voted on the 2021 infrastructure law, and the Senate's record confirmed the permitting bill's Nov. 19 passage.

Several claims could not be decided from the record. No official root-cause finding has been published for the outages, no on-record agency assessment of the dirty-bomb threat's imminence was found beyond the secretary's own testimony, and China's published readouts of the summit do not mention Iran or the Strait of Hormuz. Each statement's test, finding and sources are shown with it.

statements.speaker: Markwayne Mullin
statements.context: PolitiFact reported what Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin and two other officials told a House committee on Nov. 18 about the cause of recent outages.
statements.quote: Reported as: Mullin, FBI Deputy Director Christopher Raia and Director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton told the House Homeland Security Committee that the outages affecting the Federal Aviation Administration, the National Security Agency and private companies such as Chase , Apple and United Airlines were unrelated and not the result of hostile cyberattacks.
statements.test: True if official findings from the FAA, NSA or the companies named attribute each of the recent outages to non-hostile causes and none links them to one another. False if an official source attributes any of them to a hostile cyberattack or links them. Cannot be determined if the causes have not been published or the inquiries are open without findings.
statements.finding: As reported by Deseret News and Alhurra, officials told the committee the FAA outage came from newly installed routers overloading its telecommunications system and the others from separate maintenance and technical changes. No FAA, NSA or company root-cause finding has been published and the FBI inquiry remains open, so the claim cannot yet be decided; no source found links the outages or attributes any of them to an attack.

evidence.label: Deseret News, Mullin faces questions after FAA outage (Nov. 18)
Alhurra, U.S. officials press for answers on tech outages

statements.speaker: Markwayne Mullin

statements.finding: No on-record FBI, intelligence-community or DHS assessment of the plot's imminence, other than the secretary's own testimony, was found. A White House statement said there were "no credible threats to the homeland," and CNN's unnamed sources described the planning as "an effort to give itself options rather than an indicator of an imminent attack"; nothing found describes it as imminent.

statements.speaker: Markwayne Mullin
statements.context: In a 2021 news release, then-Rep. Markwayne Mullin, now Homeland Security Secretary, explained his vote against the bipartisan infrastructure bill.
statements.quote: Only $110 billion of this package will go towards improving actual infrastructure, like roads and bridges, and Oklahoma would only receive a small fraction of that money
statements.test: True if the 2021 bipartisan infrastructure bill's own funding for roads, bridges and major projects was about $110 billion of a larger total and Oklahoma's formula share of that was a small fraction. False if the bill's roads-and-bridges funding was substantially more than $110 billion or Oklahoma's share was large. Cannot be determined if it turns on what counts as 'actual infrastructure'.
statements.finding: The White House's Aug. 2, 2021 fact sheet says the bill invested "$110 billion of new funds for roads, bridges, and major projects" within about $550 billion of new federal spending. AskAmerica's FHWA apportionment data give Oklahoma about $4.66 billion of about $299.7 billion in FY2022-26 highway formula funds, about 1.6%. Counting baseline highway funding as "actual infrastructure" would give a larger figure than $110 billion.

evidence.label: fiscal.fhwa_program_apportionments (FHWA formula apportionments, FY2022-26, Oklahoma vs. U.S.)
evidence.sql: SELECT SUM(amount) AS total_all, SUM(CASE WHEN state_abbr='OK' THEN amount END) AS ok_total FROM fiscal.fhwa_program_apportionments

evidence.label: White House, updated fact sheet on the Bipartisan Infrastructure Investment and Jobs Act (Aug. 2, 2021)

statements.speaker: Dan Goldman
statements.context: At a Nov. 18 House Homeland Security Committee hearing, Rep. Dan Goldman described staffing at DHS and FBI cybersecurity units under the Trump administration.
statements.quote: have decimated the cybersecurity personnel that this administration entered office with
statements.test: True if official staffing figures show cybersecurity personnel at DHS (including CISA) and the FBI fell by a large share, roughly a third or more, since January 2025. False if those staffing levels are flat or higher. Cannot be determined if figures are lacking or the result turns on how 'decimated' is read.
statements.finding: OPM headcount data in AskAmerica's warehouse show CISA's workforce fell from 3,379 in January 2025 to 2,197 in September 2026, about 35%, while the FBI as a whole fell from 37,107 to 35,427, about 4.5%. No series isolates FBI cybersecurity staff, so the FBI part cannot be measured, and "decimated" has no fixed threshold.

evidence.label: officials.federal_workforce_by_agency (OPM headcount, CISA and FBI, Jan. 2025-Sept. 2026)
evidence.sql: SELECT snapshot_month, agency_subelement, SUM(headcount) hc FROM officials.federal_workforce_by_agency WHERE snapshot_month IN ('202501','202601','202608','202609','202610') AND (agency_subelement_code='HSCA' OR agency_code='HS' OR agency_subelement ILIKE '%FEDERAL BUREAU OF INV%') GROUP BY snapshot_month, agency_subelement ORDER BY agency_subelement, snapshot_month

statements.speaker: Carlos Gimenez
statements.context: At a Nov. 18 House Homeland Security Committee hearing, Rep. Carlos Gimenez described a dirty bomb.
statements.quote: simple to make and detonate
statements.test: True if official sources (NRC, DHS, CDC) describe a dirty bomb (radiological dispersal device) as relatively simple to make and set off. False if official sources describe it as difficult to make or detonate. Cannot be determined if official sources do not address its difficulty.
statements.finding: NRC and CDC fact pages describe a dirty bomb as conventional explosives combined with radioactive material that would rarely release enough radiation to kill, but do not say how easy one is to make or detonate; a 2011 Congressional Research Service report calls such devices "much simpler to build" than nuclear weapons while listing obstacles to an effective attack. These pages were read through a summarizing fetch tool, not directly, and the DHS fact sheet could not be read.

evidence.label: NRC, Dirty Bombs fact sheet
CDC, radiation emergencies overview
Congressional Research Service, R41891 Dirty Bombs: Background in Brief (2011)

statements.speaker: Michael McCaul
statements.context: At a Nov. 18 House Homeland Security Committee hearing, Rep. Michael McCaul described smuggling a dirty bomb.
statements.quote: smuggling a dirty bomb would be a relatively easy thing to do
statements.test: True if official assessments (GAO, DHS, NRC) describe smuggling a radiological device or its material into the United States as relatively easy, for example because of detection gaps. False if official assessments say detection makes it difficult. Cannot be determined if official assessments do not address it or disagree.
statements.finding: GAO's 2022 report on radiation portal monitors (GAO-22-104498) describes a delayed replacement program, high nuisance-alarm rates and an unfinished analysis of detection gaps, but does not say smuggling radiological material is relatively easy or difficult; the report page was read through a summarizing fetch tool, not directly, and older GAO covert-test reports could not be loaded. "Relatively easy" has no stated baseline.

evidence.label: GAO-22-104498, radiation portal monitor replacement (2022)

statements.speaker: Shelley Moore Capito

statements.quote: Tonight, the passage of permitting reform in the Senate finally became reality and we took a major step towards addressing the affordability concerns of the American people
statements.test: Premise only. True if the Senate record shows the permitting reform bill passed the Senate on Nov. 19, 2026. False if it did not pass or passed on a different date. Cannot be determined if the Senate record cannot be read.
statements.premise: The Senate passed the permitting reform bill on the night of Nov. 19, 2026.
statements.finding: Premise only: the Senate's roll-call list shows vote 270 on Nov. 19, 2026, "Passage, H.R. 2347, as amended," passed 62-33; the permitting package moved as an amendment to H.R. 2347. AskAmerica's warehouse holds the preceding Nov. 18 votes on the same bill (the substitute amendment, 69-27, and cloture, 65-31) but not yet the Nov. 19 passage vote. The view on affordability was not assessed.

evidence.label: law.member_roll_call_votes (Senate votes from Nov. 18, 2026)
evidence.sql: select vote_date, roll_number, vote_result, count(*) n, sum(case when vote_cast='Yea' then 1 else 0 end) yea, sum(case when vote_cast='Nay' then 1 else 0 end) nay from law.member_roll_call_votes where chamber='Senate' and vote_date>='2026-11-18' group by vote_date, roll_number, vote_result order by vote_date, roll_number

statements.speaker: Sheldon Whitehouse
statements.context: NPR reported Sen. Sheldon Whitehouse's statement about what the bipartisan permitting bill the Senate passed on Nov. 19 would require of data centers.
statements.quote: Reported as: Whitehouse also said the bill would make data centers pay for the power they use.
statements.test: True if the text of the permitting bill the Senate passed on Nov. 19, 2026 contains a provision requiring data centers or other large new electricity loads to pay for the power or grid costs they cause. False if the bill has no such provision. Cannot be determined if the bill text cannot be read or the provision's effect is ambiguous.
statements.finding: S. 5653 as introduced adds a Federal Power Act section 228 that bars shifting the incremental grid costs of data centers drawing 20 megawatts or more to other customers and requires recovery from the data center; it addresses grid costs they cause rather than power use in general. The Capito substitute that the Senate actually passed as H.R. 2347 on Nov. 19 could not be read, so whether the provision survived is unconfirmed.

evidence.label: law.bill_text_versions (text versions of S. 5653 and H.R. 2347)
evidence.sql: select version_type, version_date, url from law.bill_text_versions where congress=119 and ((bill_type='s' and bill_number=5653) or (bill_type='hr' and bill_number=2347))
